# Monash Sport Performance Dashboard

An interactive R Shiny application built with **Monash Sport** for the
ETC5543 Business Analytics Creative Activity. It brings financial and
operational Excel reports into a consistent dashboard and provides
forecasting and pricing-planning tools.

**[Open the live
dashboard](https://vicky-fengz.github.io/ETC5543-Monash-Sports/)** ·
[User guide](docs/user_guide.html) · [Developer maintainer
guide](docs/maintainer_guide.md)

**Project team:** Ayush Pandia and Ziqi Feng  
**Monash Sport mentors:** Alicia Stack and Darren McLeod  
**Academic mentor:** Minh Huynh (Monash University)

The deployed application uses **Shinylive**, so R runs in the user’s
browser. Uploaded reports are processed locally in that browser session;
the published site does not receive or store report data. Monash Sport’s
confidential source workbooks are **not included** in this repository.

## Dashboard features

| Page | What it provides | Source reports |
|----|----|----|
| **Executive Dashboard** | Three fixed presentation-ready sections: **Overview** (financial KPIs, four charts, summary and insights), **Site** (visits, memberships, growth, site finances and rankings) and **Venues** (attendance, facility hire, casual wages, merchandise/equipment revenue and insights). Includes **Year Review**, two-year **Comparison**, chart hover readouts and full-screen **Presentation View**. | Monthly Site, Detailed Site and Venues Tracking reports, depending on section |
| **Overview** | Organisation-wide income, expenses, budget variance and revenue performance | Monthly Site Reports |
| **Site Comparison** | Site-level financial comparisons and facility breakdowns | Monthly Site and Detailed Site Reports |
| **Site Detail** | Visits, membership and enrolment measures for an individual reporting unit | Detailed Site Reports |
| **Venues Operations** | Attendance, facility/court hire, memberships, online sales, merchandise, finance and casual workforce | Venues Tracking Reports |
| **Forecasting** | 3-, 6- and 12-month income/expense forecasts, wage and pricing scenarios, and downloads | Monthly Site Reports, optionally Venues Tracking Reports |
| **Data** | Workbook upload and validation, warning review, saved data and cleaned-table export | Supported `.xlsx`, `.xls` and dashboard `.rds` files |

The three Executive sections use **fixed charts**, not the old *Choose
Visuals* workflow. Detailed pages retain their own filters. Missing
reported months or years remain gaps rather than being treated as zero;
supported charts show exact values on hover. For design decisions see
[Dashboard design](docs/dashboard_design.md).

## Quick start

**GitHub repository:** [Monash Sport Performance Dashboard](https://github.com/vicky-fengz/ETC5543-Monash-Sports)

**Use the live application:** Open the
[dashboard](https://vicky-fengz.github.io/ETC5543-Monash-Sports/), go to
**Data**, and upload supported workbooks. To try it without confidential
reports, use the **synthetic** workbooks in `data/sample/`.

**Run locally:** Install R 4.4 (the project was built with R 4.4.3) and
RStudio. Clone/download the repository and run from its root:

``` r
renv::restore()
shiny::runApp()
```

The package versions are recorded in `renv.lock`. For the full import
and upload workflow, file naming, warnings, saved-data format and
templates, see [Maintainer guide: data
upload](docs/maintainer_guide.md#data-upload-and-review-workflow) and
the [user guide](docs/user_guide.html).

## Data sources and privacy

The application supports three report families:

| Report family | Main outputs |
|----|----|
| **Monthly Site Reports** | Income, expenses, budgets, discounts and revenue reconciliations |
| **Detailed Site / Business Unit Reports** | Site finance, Direct/Indirect visits, memberships and enrolments |
| **Venues Tracking Reports** | Attendance, hire revenue and transactions, workforce hours/wages, online sales and merchandise/equipment measures |

Uploads are validated before being used in charts. Imported records
retain source-file, worksheet and cell-position metadata to help
reconcile figures. The [data dictionary](docs/data_dictionary.md)
defines the cleaned tables; [Excel templates](docs/excel_templates.md)
document required workbook layouts.

The workbooks under `data/sample/` use artificial figures and must
**never** be treated as actual Monash Sport results. Don’t commit
original reports, exported confidential `.rds` files or screenshots
containing real values. The live app does not keep uploads between
sessions; **Save current data** produces a local `.rds` file that must
be handled as confidential data.

## Architecture at a glance

``` text
Excel workbooks → import → cleaning and validation → standardised data
                                                   ↓
                       shared calculations and reporting context
                                                   ↓
                      page modules → charts, KPIs and forecasts
```

| Location | Responsibility |
|----|----|
| [`app.R`](app.R) | Starts the application, connects navigation and shares uploaded data across pages |
| [`R/data/`](R/data/) | Source-specific Excel extraction, cleaning, validation and extensible metric handling |
| [`R/calculations.R`](R/calculations.R) and [`R/reporting_context.R`](R/reporting_context.R) | Shared financial calculations, reporting years, sites and source context |
| [`R/mod_*.R`](R/) | Individual page UI, server calculations and reactive interactions |
| [`R/plots.R`](R/plots.R) and [`R/forecast_plots.R`](R/forecast_plots.R) | Charts, legends and plotted series |
| [`R/forecasting.R`](R/forecasting.R) | Forecast and business-planning models |
| [`R/config.R`](R/config.R) and [`www/styles.css`](www/styles.css) | Branding, constants and responsive styling |
| [`tests/`](tests/) | Regression, parser, cross-page and chart checks |
| [`deploy/`](deploy/) and [`.github/workflows/`](.github/workflows/) | Browser build, continuous integration and GitHub Pages deployment |

**For the full file-by-file map**, including
`mod_executive_dashboard.R`, all data importers and the tests to update
for each change, use the [developer handover and file
map](docs/maintainer_guide.md#developer-handover-and-file-map).

## Maintaining the application

This repository is designed for an incoming Monash Sport developer to
take over. Start with
[`docs/maintainer_guide.md`](docs/maintainer_guide.md) before changing
data aggregation rules or source templates.

| If you need to… | Where to start |
|----|----|
| **Upload the next reporting year** | [New reporting years](docs/maintainer_guide.md#adding-future-report-years) (normally no code change) |
| **Support a changed Excel template** | [Importer maintenance steps](docs/maintainer_guide.md#b-an-excel-workbook-changes-its-column-names-or-structure) |
| **Add a site, facility or new measure** | [Adding reporting categories](docs/maintainer_guide.md#c-add-a-new-site-business-unit-facility-or-activity) |
| **Change a KPI, plot or hover readout** | [Dashboard change procedure](docs/maintainer_guide.md#d-change-a-kpi-chart-hover-feature-or-executive-insight) |
| **Change the forecast** | [Forecast maintenance](docs/maintainer_guide.md#e-update-forecasting-or-business-planning-assumptions) |
| **Diagnose incorrect totals** | [Calculation safeguards](docs/maintainer_guide.md#important-calculation-and-reporting-rules) |
| **Release an update** | [Troubleshooting and release checklist](docs/maintainer_guide.md#troubleshooting-and-release-checklist) |

The most important safeguards are to distinguish **unreported data from
zero**, avoid summing YTD totals together with their monthly/detail
components, and avoid summing successive membership snapshots. A wage
budget difference must use a clearly stated sign convention. More detail
and exceptions are in the maintainer guide.

## Testing and deployment

Run the basic regression suite from the project root:

``` r
source("tests/run_tests.R")
```

Run the synthetic-workbook end-to-end checks before releasing:

``` r
source("tests/run_sample_tests.R")
```

For sequential debugging, first run
`Sys.setenv(MONASH_SPORT_TEST_WORKERS = "1")`. Authorised maintainers
can use `tests/run_full_tests.R` with the confidential workbooks kept on
their own computer, never in the repository. See [Testing
instructions](docs/maintainer_guide.md#testing) for expected coverage
and how to update intentional snapshot changes.

GitHub Actions tests and builds the Shinylive site; the deployment
workflow publishes changes from `main` to GitHub Pages. Review the code
diff, run tests, and check the deployed application with **synthetic**
reports. See the [deployment
guide](docs/maintainer_guide.md#3-publish-a-new-version).

## Report, presentation and licence

The final project report and presentation are available below:

- [Project report (PDF)](report/report.pdf)
- [Project report (HTML)](report/index.html)
- [Project presentation](slides/slides.html)

The project report and presentation are Quarto files. To rebuild them
from the project root with Quarto installed:

``` bash
quarto render report/report.qmd
quarto render slides/slides.qmd
```

The report files live in [`report/`](report/) and the slides in
[`slides/`](slides/). The application code and documentation use the
[MIT Licence](LICENSE). Monash University/Monash Sport names, logos,
brand assets and confidential reporting data are **not** covered by that
licence; bundled third-party Quarto resources retain their own licences.
